newsitem.title: ROMANIA: U.S. fund eyes Romania's troubled Credit Bank.
newsitem.headline: U.S. fund eyes Romania's troubled Credit Bank.

text.p: The American National Group (ANG) of the U.S. said on Wednesday it planned to take over the assets and liabilities of Romania's troubled private Credit Bank SA, with plans to restructure it and make it profitable.
Last month, the U.S. company announced a similar deal with Romania's other troubled bank Dacia Felix, whose assets and liabilities would also be transfered to the ANG.

Romania's central bank (BNR) stripped the private Dacia Felix and Credit Bank of their banking licences in April over their deteriorated financial position. Both banks contested the BNR measure in court.
The deals need central bank approval to become effective.

"We hope the central bank will approve the deals, as they are the largest creditor of Dacia Felix and an important one in Credit Bank," Ronald Gutenman, ANG vice-president and senior investment officer, told a news conference.
Last year, the BNR asked authorities to decide on the two banks' liquidation or reorganisation.

Gutenman said they would go ahead with the project even if the two banks would not get back their licences as the U.S. group -- which manages the capital of U.S. pension funds and trusts -- had signed contracts with both troubled banks in May.

An ANG press release described the company as a "discretionary capital management" also known under the name of American National Realty Advisers based in Dallas, Texas, with the State Street Bank & Trust Co. of Boston, Massachusetts being its custodian bank.
ANG was set up in August 1994 to manage pension funds' capital and specialised in real estate deals, it said.

Gutenman said ANG would set up a commercial company in Romania, the American National Commercial Group (ANCG), to manage the funds needed to cover the difference between the bank's assets and liabilities.
"We anticipate seeing profits in 36-40 months," he said.
No value was given for the two deals.
Gutenman said ANG would ask international accountants Coopers & Lybrand and Deloitte & Touche to audit the two banks.

"When the price is known we will put this money into the accounts of the new ANCG to help the banks restructure, pay their debts as well as recover debts due to them," ANCG president Alexandru Puscaciuc said.
